parts.note: a venomous snake that spreads a hood of skin behind its head before it strikes, read as if a masked assassin

explanation.surface: A masked assassin stalks the night.
explanation.definitionFit: This snake is famous for flaring a hood and for its deadly venom.

clue.text: Greek centre replaced by French in Polish port

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Greek has new letters placed between its two letters, standing where a centre would be

parts.note: dans is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A Greek is swapped for a Frenchman at the heart of a Baltic harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French in' is not a Frenchman but the French word for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Baltic city on the Vistula delta is a major shipping harbour of Poland.

explanation.surface: A thief pinches just a fraction of a measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF-INCH is cockney rhyming slang: half-inch rhymes with pinch, which means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the phrase means pinch, i.e. steal, and literally it is a small length of 1.27 cm.

parts.note: suggests a man dressing as a woman, but means a woman whose job is to pretend to be other people on stage

explanation.surface: A drag artist takes the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs roles in plays or films impersonates characters for a living.

clue.text: They may be hung and drawn, but not necessarily quartered

definitions.text: They may be hung and drawn, but not necessarily quartered

parts.words: They may be hung and drawn, but not necessarily quartered
parts.note: plays on the old punishment of hanging, drawing and quartering; window drapes are hung on rails and drawn open or shut

explanation.surface: Traitors face a grisly medieval execution, though perhaps spared the final cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Window drapes are hung from a rail and drawn across to close them.

explanation.surface: A movie backer is named.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is Coppola's 1972 mafia classic; the other sense is a person who sponsors a child at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous mafia movie and also a baptismal sponsor who vouches for a child.

clue.text: One may bowl a maiden over, or get a wicket

definitions.text: One may bowl a maiden over

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls a maiden over or takes a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden over is an over with no runs scored; here 'bowl a maiden over' means sweep a young woman off her feet. A catch held by a fielder dismisses a batsman, i.e. gets a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A desirable partner may dazzle a young woman, and a well-held ball in the field dismisses a batsman.

explanation.surface: Something was stuck on artificially.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes or labels are attached by being placed on, and a feigned manner is affected or false.

clue.text: See a letter goes to the agent

parts.note: E is a letter of the alphabet
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Look: a letter is delivered to the secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to notice or glimpse it.

clue.text: Side to side movement by a footballer, perhaps

definitions.text: Side to side movement by a footballer, perhaps

parts.words: Side to side movement by a footballer, perhaps
parts.note: sounds like a lateral pass or dribble, but the sides are clubs and the movement is a player switching teams

explanation.surface: A footballer dribbles from one flank to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A player's move from one club to another is a deal made between teams.

explanation.surface: Begin by displaying something at its best.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart on a journey is to begin it, and a frame or contrast enhances an item by highlighting it.

parts.note: kin are one's relatives, a family group

explanation.surface: Something resembles a family clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Things alike in nature are related, as relatives are.

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
lists are catalogues

explanation.surface: A range of pens is catalogued for authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool, fitting 'writers', but it is a pigpen. Old writing instruments with points were also so named, which explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for pointed writing implements, or for authors noted for elegant prose.

clue.text: Aim always, say, to do one's best

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: say marks that the word for always is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Always aim to try your hardest.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive or make a real effort is to try as hard as possible.

clue.text: Cunning required in any lawless state

indicators.note: in places the word for cunning within the clue word any

parts.note: taken as written
arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: Craftiness is needed in any country without laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos with no government or rule of law is a total breakdown of order.

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
tiring means becoming weary, losing interest

explanation.surface: Someone backs off, bored once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy or going to bed, a person pulling back from company is reserved.

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of lobster are made anew

explanation.surface: A pair of newly caught crustaceans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' looks like a pair of lobsters, but it is a verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or prop up something is to support it.

parts.note: out means away or off, as in going out
a break is a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden beginning of war or disease is its eruption.

clue.text: One isn't put out by it, but it's a strain

definitions.text: One isn't put out by it, but it's a strain

parts.words: One isn't put out by it, but it's a strain
parts.note: plays on being stressed versus being put out, i.e. annoyed; a pull of strain or stress is meant

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm under pressure, though it is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress or tightness in a situation or a rope is strain.

clue.text: Support for those in temporary accommodation

definitions.text: Support for those in temporary accommodation

parts.words: Support for those in temporary accommodation
parts.note: reads like aid for the homeless, but means the upright that holds up campers' canvas shelters

explanation.surface: Help is offered to people living in temporary housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Campers' canvas shelters are held up by an upright stake.

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter, in this down entry

parts.note: women are females

explanation.surface: Bare-chested women are a worrying portent.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign of things to come, often of trouble.

clue.text: Record is broken by the winner

explanation.surface: A record is broken by the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a world record broken, but it is the noun for a recording medium; the winner of a race breaks the finishing line ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic strip is a recording medium, and the finishing ribbon is broken by the first runner home.

clue.text: Key operators may strike against it

definitions.text: Key operators may strike against it

parts.words: Key operators may strike against it
parts.note: suggests important workers going on strike, but means typists whose keys hit the roller of a typewriter

explanation.surface: Essential workers might walk out in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: On a typewriter the keys strike paper held against this roller.

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of evils are in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Weird wickedness and masks go together.
explanation.definitionFit: Face coverings conceal identity and so act as masks.

clue.text: A few lines apparently expressing hostility

parts.note: a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A short poem seems to voice opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' is a link: read the answer as A VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed or strongly disinclined shows dislike.

parts.note: sounds like someone short of garments, but means a naked runner at a public event

explanation.surface: Someone is low on things to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dashes naked across a sports pitch is unclothed.

explanation.surface: Someone heads out on brief strolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Players take goes in games, and a stroll round the garden is a brief outing.

clue.text: Give two pounds, nothing more, for a Ninja Turtle

parts.note: donate means give
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, so two of them make LL
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Donate a couple of quid and no more to a cartoon reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: The four Ninja Turtles are named after Renaissance artists; this one also names the Florentine sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cartoon reptiles, named after the Florentine Renaissance sculptor.
